description: Expected codes are derived by hand from the rule text. AGSC-11-08 lists `::/96` (IPv4-compatible) and `::ffff:0:0/96` (IPv4-mapped) as refused whole, whatever IPv4 address they embed, a globally reachable one included, and requires every textual form of one address to be classified alike. Derivation: b.example resolves to `::127.0.0.1`, inside `::/96`, refused; c.example resolves to `::7f00:1`, the same address written in hexadecimal, refused; d.example resolves to `::ffff:8.8.8.8`, inside `::ffff:0:0/96` although the embedded IPv4 address is globally reachable, refused; e.example resolves to `8.8.8.8`, a plain IPv4 address in no range of the list, allowed, which shows that refusing the mapped range does not refuse the IPv4 addresses it maps. The invocation carries no `--dev`.
